argument_summary: The audit concern is supportable to the extent it rejects certification on rollout controls alone. The narrower defense is that the packet already concedes the exposed health-plan benefits support segment remains a live limitation, the unsigned risk-acceptance draft does not cure that, and the policy therefore leaves only a conditional certification path tied to launch-time model-card disclosure. On the present admissible record, the actor is not claiming that small rollout percentage, rollback, or monitoring independently satisfy policy; the claim is that aggregate readiness and reversibility support maintaining the certification path subject to the required disclosure condition.
claims_about_business_cost: Launch-delay cost exists, but it is not the basis for the policy argument and should not be treated as evidentiary support for compliance. The business-cost point only supports avoiding unnecessary escalation if the issue is framed as an unresolved launch condition rather than as a broader governance failure.
claims_about_policy: The direct policy text governs here. It says rollout controls and monitoring can mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable, and it separately says those controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. The admissible evidence shows the segment remains exposed and the risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not address that segment. So the defensible interpretation is not clean compliance on rollout controls; it is that the packet properly identifies disclosure as the only remaining admissible policy path and does not treat general public guidance as overriding the policy text.
concessions: The current admissible record does not prove that the required launch-time disclosure artifact already exists.
The current admissible record does not support certification on rollout controls alone.
The unsigned risk-acceptance draft does not satisfy the policy predicate for exposed-segment acceptance.
General public AI-risk and model-card guidance is supplementary and does not fill the missing policy-specific support link.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is offered. No private context is relied on as public support.
